findings.message: This JSX is constructed inside a try block, which does not catch what the author almost certainly means to catch. Writing JSX builds a plain description object and renders nothing, so React runs the component later, long after this try has returned. The only errors this catch can see are the rare ones thrown while building the description itself, never the rendering errors the pattern is reaching for. Move the JSX out of the try and wrap the component in an error boundary, which is the mechanism that does catch errors during rendering.
